title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: At step 3 of one request, the model uses a calendar result it received at step 1. What makes that result available to the model at step 3?

options.text: The model stores the result internally and recalls it later
The program includes the result in the input of that call
The calendar tool re-sends the result to the model itself
The training of the model already contains the result

items.stem: A request takes two model calls. The fixed part of the context (system prompt, tool descriptions and question) is 500 tokens. Call 1 outputs a 30-token tool request. The tool returns a 1,000-token result, and call 2 writes the final answer. What is the total number of input tokens across the two calls, if each call is sent the full transcript so far?
Your assistant must answer from a 400-page laser cutter manual, and most questions need only one or two pages. Which design keeps cost per request lowest while still finding the right page?

options.text: Paste the whole manual into every request's context
Give the model a one-paragraph summary of the manual
Give the model a search tool that returns the best pages
Give the model only the manual's table of contents

items.stem: A student passes laser cutter training on Monday and returns on Thursday in a new chat. In one sentence, what must the assistant's program do so that the assistant knows about the training?
A long chat nears the context limit. The program asks the model to summarize it and continues in a fresh context holding only that summary. What is the main risk of this approach?

options.text: The summary may leave out a detail needed later
The model permanently loses its ability to use tools
The discarded text is billed again on every later call
The context window is smaller in every later session
